collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. The current OpenHands repository path was resolved from its public GitHub redirect notice. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, agents, models, tools, workflows or target systems were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: Git info probe on the shared bash-events socket can resolve with another client's command output
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled cross-client command-result misrouting through a shared event socket
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenHands Canvas and Agent Server shared event transport; no model-provider fault or live provider execution established.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic browser-side test pairs a pending local repository-information probe with another client's command output, which is parsed as the local repository and branch. A later project comment says the shared socket runner was removed, so the path likely does not remain on current main. This is wrong-source result transfer and use between intentional clients, not independently verified autonomous agents.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: In-flight load-older-events page from a previous conversation merges into the next conversation's event store after switching
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reproduced cross-conversation event ownership and rendering failure
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenHands web event-store pagination; no model-provider fault established.
selected_records.assessment: A reported and independently reproduced UI race splices conversation A's older events into conversation B's store, where they are rendered and can enter history-seeding logic until reload. This is cross-conversation message transfer and use in client state, not an exchange among distinct autonomous participants.

selected_records.title: [Bug]: Launcher never creates TMUX_TMPDIR, so local Agent Canvas instances share one tmux server and reset each other's terminals
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported cross-instance terminal reset caused by an unintentionally shared local tmux server
selected_records.provider_attribution: OpenHands Agent Canvas launcher and local tmux isolation; the reporter identifies Claude Code as an assistant but does not authenticate a second autonomous participant.
selected_records.assessment: The report says starting or restarting one local Canvas instance resets another instance's terminal, after which its agent observes an exit and may rerun the command. Project triage agrees the launcher isolation gap is real but requested scope evidence. This is shared-runtime interference, not task-result exchange or verified rogue coordination.

selected_records.title: Bound the delegator's transcript read to the delegated turn
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported standing delegator capability to read later private expert-thread output beyond the delegated turn
selected_records.provider_attribution: AutoGPT Platform delegation transcript authorization; no model-provider execution evidence.
selected_records.assessment: A code-review follow-up says a delegating session can keep polling the target expert's visible thread and retrieve an answer produced days after the delegated turn. This is a confidentiality and result-routing design gap in an intentional delegation feature, not a documented live incident or independently authenticated autonomous exchange.

selected_records.title: Persist parent-session provenance for sub-sessions and isolate polling scope
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: potential same-user cross-session polling, waiting and cancellation caused by missing parent provenance
selected_records.provider_attribution: AutoGPT Platform sub-session provenance and authorization design; no model-provider execution evidence.
selected_records.assessment: The design issue says unrelated same-user sessions without an expert identifier may address another ordinary session's sub-session because parent provenance is not persisted. It documents an authorization gap but supplies no concrete runtime episode, transferred output or downstream use.

selected_records.title: AutoPilot keeps using a stale integration token for up to 5 minutes after a credential is upgraded
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported single-agent credential-freshness failure after reauthorization
selected_records.provider_attribution: AutoGPT Platform integration-token cache and GitHub credential use; no GitHub or model-provider fault established.
selected_records.assessment: A user-session timeline reports the agent continuing to use a stale integration token for several minutes after reauthorization because invalidation happened in another process. The agent then incorrectly described the credential upgrade as partial. This is a single-agent permission-freshness boundary, not multi-agent result exchange.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. OpenHands records preserve concrete wrong-context command or message transfer and downstream use, while AutoGPT records preserve delegation-scope and credential-freshness boundaries. All episodes were already public and concern framework clients, UI stores, configured sessions or one agent rather than independently verified autonomous participants acting outside operator authorization.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
The retired All-Hands-AI/OpenHands path was not counted as an empty search; the pass used the current public OpenHands/OpenHands repository.
Issue bodies and comments are public tracker evidence, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Configured clients, conversations, sessions and expert/delegator roles are not independently verified autonomous participants.
Open issue state does not prove a vulnerable current release, public deployment or continuing agent activity.
No code, package, reproduction, agent, model, tool, workflow or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original real-run exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization rather than reflecting shared transport, UI state, runtime isolation, transcript scope or stale credentials.
redactions: No executable reproduction bodies, commands, tokens, personal addresses, private logs or tool payloads are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanisms at a domain level.
